title: Verifier‑Grounded, Preregistered Paired Study of LLM‑Generated Network Configurations (CAND‑2026‑001): Why a Shared‑Candidate Confirmatory Test Collapsed to 120/120
abstract: Estimand and design (explicit): this preregistered confirmatory test evaluated the paired estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline under generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (CAND‑2026‑001‑NetConfig‑Semantic‑v1, preregistration SHA‑256 7db1663cf3982c8ea1e16c3dd7c0348f356bb4cbe3978ecc75bb59fdedb71a37). Using a deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) we compared a deterministic template baseline to a single canonical LLM generator (declared_model_version = gpt‑5‑mini) on N = 120 intent→configuration tasks. Result (artifact‑grounded): baseline = 120/120 verifier passes; guarded (gpt‑5‑mini, shared candidate) = 120/120 verifier passes; paired difference = 0.00; 95% bootstrap percentile CI [0.00, 0.00] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729); exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. We (1) publish complete execution and scoring artifacts with SHA‑256 fingerprints to permit byte‑for‑byte reruns (see execution/execution_manifest.json in the artifact bundle), (2) show—using archived shared candidate files and per‑episode validator traces—why the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics deterministically produced the degenerate contingency (identical inputs + deterministic validator), and (3) provide artifact‑grounded, runnable experimental modifications (independent_per_condition sampling, multi‑seed replication, validator diversity) that answer the operational question of independent generative reliability while preserving reproducibility. The immutable initial master prompt is archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba).

sections.introduction: Translating operator intent into device configuration is a core NetOps task whose correctness has immediate safety and availability consequences. Deterministic offline validators (reachability/ACL/routing analyzers) provide auditable oracles for pre‑deployment checks; coupling generative systems to such validators yields operationally meaningful generate–validate–repair workflows. We preregistered (CAND‑2026‑001) a paired confirmatory comparison framed to test a clearly specified estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline using generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate. The aim was to publish an exhaustive, artifact‑anchored run and to diagnose, from those artifacts, what the preregistered confirmatory statistics validly show and do not show for deployment decisions.
sections.related_work: Verifier‑grounded NetOps evaluations and intent→config studies emphasize generate–validate–repair and differ methodologically by sampling semantics (single canonical candidate vs independent per‑condition), repair budget, and validator scope. Prior work shows (i) iterative repair yields most gains in early iterations and (ii) independent per‑condition sampling is required to estimate stochastic generative reliability. Deterministic validators such as Batfish and related control‑plane analyzers are standard operational oracles (see Brown et al., Batfish evolution; doi:10.1145/3603269.3604866) and motivate our verifier‑anchored design and artifact publication requirements.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and artifacts. The full preregistration (CAND‑2026‑001‑NetConfig‑Semantic‑v1) was frozen prior to model calls (SHA‑256 7db1663c...). The declared generator was gpt‑5‑mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 a40e96e2...), adapter hosted_netops_gvr_v1; validator deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (version 5.0). Confirmatory plan: N = 120 paired tasks (40 per topology class), generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate, one canonical LLM candidate per task reused for both baseline and guarded scoring episodes, primary analysis = paired_binary_analysis_v1 (bootstrap 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729), primary estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. Key archived references (byte‑identical): execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt (SHA‑256 8f38c8be...), execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json (SHA‑256 0d56c1ad...), execution/execution_manifest.json (full manifest and per‑file SHA‑256s).

Required reviewer mapping (short boxed table). This explicit mapping was requested and is provided here (artifact‑anchored):

- Operational question practitioners need: independent per‑condition generative reliability = P(LLM_output passes validator) when LLM candidates are drawn independently per condition. (Not the preregistered estimand.)
- Preregistered estimand tested here: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline under shared_initial_candidate — tests whether a deterministic validator yields different pass/fail outcomes for identical canonical inputs across conditions. (See preregistration SHA‑256 7db1663c... and shared responses at execution/responses/*-shared-initial.txt.)
- Causal reason the confirmatory test collapsed: identical canonical candidate per pair + deterministic validator ⇒ identical validator outcome for both episodes; archived evidence: matched shared_initial candidate SHA‑256s and matching validator traces (execution/scoring/*.json) produced n_11 = 120, n_10 = n_01 = n_00 = 0. (See analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv.)

Execution constraints. The confirmatory run used the single canonical candidate per pair (model_calls_used = 120; planned maximum_model_calls = 240). The run logs, provider call traces, and full call cache are archived (execution/provider_calls/*.json, execution/call_cache/*) to permit exact reruns and contamination audits.
sections.results: Confirmatory, artifact‑grounded outcome (exact counts from archived scoring files): complete_pair_count = 120. Baseline verifier passes = 120/120. Guarded (gpt‑5‑mini, shared initial candidate) verifier passes = 120/120. Paired 2×2 contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv): n_11 = 120, n_10 = 0, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0. Primary estimator = mean(guarded_i − baseline_i) = 0.00. Bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) 95% percentile CI [0.00, 0.00]. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. Representative validator traces are archived (e.g., execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json SHA‑256 0d56c1ad...), showing parsed_command_count, required_command_count, normalized_configuration, and validation_after.valid = true for those canonical candidates. Provider call accounting: model_calls_used = 120; no infrastructure failures or retries were required. Contamination heuristics (preregistered string‑overlap thresholds) flagged no confirmatory items; full provider traces are included for external audit.
sections.discussion:
What the confirmatory statistics legitimately support. The preregistered test correctly answers the preregistered estimand: whether a deterministic validator treats identical canonical inputs differently under two scoring episodes. The archived artifacts show identical inputs were used per pair; therefore identical pass/fail outcomes were necessarily observed. What the confirmatory statistics do not support. They do not estimate independent generative reliability (the deployment‑relevant probability that independently sampled LLM outputs satisfy the validator). That latter estimand requires independent_per_condition sampling or multi‑seed per condition; the archived pipeline and artifacts permit deterministic reruns under those semantics without changing task definitions. Runnable, artifact‑grounded next steps (no new experiments invented here): (A) independent_per_condition rerun — generate separate seeds per condition per task and rescore using the archived validator (preserves reproducibility via the execution manifest and per‑file SHA‑256 fingerprints), (B) multi‑seed replication (K≥3) per condition to estimate per‑condition pass probabilities with bootstrap CIs, (C) validator diversification to reduce validator–task coupling (run an independent verifier and report intersection/union pass rates). All files and exact paths required to perform these reruns are in the submission bundle (execution/* and analysis/* with SHA‑256s).

Threats to validity (artifact‑anchored): internal — shared_initial semantics intentionally removed generation variance; construct — template‑tight tasks + single validator can overstate success for template‑aligned candidates; external — single model (gpt‑5‑mini) and synthetic tasks limit generalization; conclusion validity — degenerate contingency yields trivial inferential outputs that must not be overinterpreted. These are documented via the archived traces and the preregistration.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered, verifier‑grounded paired experiment and published exhaustive execution and scoring artifacts with per‑file SHA‑256 fingerprints to permit byte‑for‑byte reproduction. Under the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics both baseline and the single canonical gpt‑5‑mini candidates passed the deterministic validator on all N = 120 tasks (baseline = 120/120; guarded = 120/120; paired diff = 0.00; CI [0.00,0.00]; McNemar p = 1.0). Archived artifacts demonstrate that the degeneracy is a direct, auditable consequence of the preregistered generation semantics (identical candidate per pair) combined with a deterministic validator. To answer the operational question practitioners typically need (independent generative reliability) one must rerun the archived pipeline under independent_per_condition or multi‑seed sampling; we provide the exact artifact paths and checksums required to perform those deterministic reruns. All artifacts and the immutable initial master prompt are archived for external audit (provenance/master_prompt.txt SHA‑256 1872df1e...).

limitations: Controlled synthetic tasks: programmatic templates produced narrow required_sequences and workflow_policies that favour canonical solutions and limit external generalizability to heterogeneous operational intents.

Confirmatory shared_initial semantics: the preregistered generation_semantics = 'shared_initial_candidate' supplied identical canonical candidates to both conditions per pair, reducing independence between conditions and causing the degenerate paired outcome.

Single canonical seed for confirmatory test: the primary analysis used one canonical seed per task; preregistered exploratory multi‑seed analyses (seeds_1..4) were not included in the confirmatory inference reported here.

Validator–task coupling: the deterministic validator enforces constraints encoded in the task templates, which can increase pass rates for template‑aligned candidates and reduce construct validity for open distributions.

Possible training‑data exposure: preregistered contamination heuristics found no flags under chosen thresholds, but absence of a flag is not proof of zero exposure to related artifacts in model pretraining.

Single‑model, single‑validator run: results apply only to gpt‑5‑mini under the recorded configuration and deterministic_netops_validator_v5; they do not generalize across model families, agentic pipelines, or other validators.
